kurz: Crisp means: the cells still stick together and are plump with water.
bild_im_kopf: Like a fresh apple compared with an old one: the cells are plump and hold together.
bedeutung: Bite comes from the glue between the cells and the water pressure inside them. Heat dissolves the glue; lying around for a long time lets the water escape.
was_passiert: Short, hot cooking dissolves only a little glue. Acid in the cooking water slows the softening further; baking soda speeds it up. Limp vegetables firm up again in cold water.
faustregeln: Cook briefly and [[abschrecken|refresh]] in cold water.
Put limp lettuce or carrots in cold water for 15 minutes.

praxis.text: Stir-fried vegetables: small pieces, very hot, a few minutes.
